stats.text:
A creature can grapple another creature. Characters typically grapple by using an {ref:glossary/unarmed-strike}. Many monsters have special attacks that allow them to quickly grapple prey. However a grapple is initiated, it follows these rules. *See also* "Unarmed Strike" and "{ref:condition/grappled}."

***Grappled Condition.*** Successfully grappling a creature gives it the {ref:condition/grappled} condition.

***One Grapple per Hand.*** A creature must have a hand free to grapple another creature. Some stat blocks and game effects allow a creature to grapple using a tentacle, a maw, or another body part. Whatever part a grappler uses, it can grapple only one creature at a time with that part, and the grappler can't use that part to target another creature unless it ends the grapple.

***Ending a Grapple.*** A {ref:condition/grappled} creature can use its action to make a Strength (Athletics) or Dexterity (Acrobatics) check against the grapple's escape DC, ending the condition on itself on a success. The condition also ends if the grappler has the {ref:condition/incapacitated} condition or if the distance between the {ref:condition/grappled} target and the grappler exceeds the grapple's range. In addition, the grappler can release the target at any time (no action required).
